correctness.rationale: The Frobenius class-multiplication formula gives 1 in C^3 iff the exact character sum is nonzero. The committed exact trace certificate reports precisely classes 12,17,18 as zeros; an independent fresh complex reconstruction from the committed 74x74 irreducible block reproduced near-zero sums for those three classes. Classes 17 and 18 are an inverse nonreal pair, so C^2 does not contain 1 and C^3 does not contain 1, yielding e(PSp_6(3))>=4. Class 12 is real and is not needed for that lower bound.

evidence: General product-of-classes machinery does not supply these exact zeros for PSp_6(3).

final_claim: For PSp_6(3), the Frobenius cubic class-product character sum vanishes on classes 12, 17 and 18; the nonreal inverse pair 17/18 therefore has no identity in its square or cube, so e(PSp_6(3))>=4 and the universal exponent-3 claim for q=3 mod 4 is false.
